prompt: The client asks: "Should we enter the Canadian market?" Fact sheet: the Canadian market is worth $400M and growing 3% a year; entry would cost $60M; expected profit is $12M a year, a 5-year payback; the client's hurdle is a 3-year payback; two incumbents hold 70% share; the client is headquartered in Chicago. Which is the best recommendation?

options.text: The client should not enter Canada now. Payback would be 5 years against a 3-year hurdle, in a market growing only 3% a year where two incumbents hold 70%. The main risk is that a partnership could change the economics, so the next step is to test whether a partnership could cut the $60M entry cost.
options.feedback: Right. It leads with the answer, backs it with the numbers that matter, and gives a risk and a next step.

options.text: On one hand, payback would be 5 years against a 3-year hurdle, in a market growing only 3% a year where two incumbents hold 70%. On the other hand, there is the risk that a partnership could change the economics. It depends on the client's priorities, so I'd want more analysis before committing either way.
options.feedback: This never takes a position. Commit to an answer, then name the risk.

options.text: The client should not enter Canada now. The client is headquartered in Chicago, close to Canada. Payback would be 5 years against a 3-year hurdle, in a market growing only 3% a year where two incumbents hold 70%.
options.feedback: It leads with the answer, but pads it with a fact that doesn't bear on the decision.

options.text: The client should not enter Canada now. Canada just isn't attractive for the client right now.
options.feedback: It gives an answer but none of the numbers from the fact sheet to back it.
